input: patterns contains nonempty ASCII lowercase strings and word is an ASCII lowercase string, possibly empty. Duplicate pattern entries are allowed. Collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse/accessor-backed collections. Strings are ordinary/primitive strings. Every collection length and computed allocation size fits [0,4294967295], with padded sizes explicitly included. No concurrent mutation or built-in monkey-patching is allowed. Preconditions are not runtime-checked, and allocation/resource capacity or completion is not guaranteed by declared bounds. Python integer inputs are plain int, excluding bool.
return: Number of pattern entries that occur as a contiguous substring of word; each duplicate entry contributes separately.
mutation_aliasing: Inputs and caller-held aliases remain unchanged; working state is private. The Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: Only ASCII substring matching and a count at most the number of patterns are used. All integer inputs/intermediates remain within [-9007199254740991,9007199254740991]; no bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: O(P+(W+1)*T+1) worst-case time for P patterns, word length W and total pattern length T, and O(1) auxiliary space. Every substring comparison is explicit in the charged helper; no runtime search algorithm is hidden. Bounds include ordinary built-in operations/allocations and assume bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time indexing, amortized append/pop and any explicitly stated hash/sort behavior.

helpers.name: contains_text
helpers.contract: Tests each possible starting index and compares contiguous ASCII characters until mismatch or full match. Does not slice or allocate substrings.
helpers.cost: O((W+1)*(L+1)) worst-case time and O(1) auxiliary space for text length W and pattern length L; complete helper charged. Its complete definition is 306 UTF-8 bytes; separator newlines count toward total source bytes.

source_accounting: The complete standalone source is 535 UTF-8 bytes, including every helper, Solution wrapper, signature, loop, built-in call, annotation/comment, whitespace and terminal newline. Helpers are fully charged per candidate, not free shared libraries. No imports, runtime-generated implementations or hidden source expansion are used. Any eventual judge-interface adapter is additional charged source.
